opta.source: The Analyst Liverpool vs Man City preview (Matchday 6, Oct 2026), 10,000 sims; echoed by beIN Sports 'The Numbers Game' 9 Oct 2026. NOTE: the brief's lead of 'Man City 29.8%' looks misattributed; 29.8% is Coventry's Opta figure v Newcastle.

odds.source: Paddy Power via Racing Post: Liverpool 17/10, Draw 13/5, Man City 29/20 (de-vigged approx L 35 / D 26 / C 39). Football365: Liverpool 8/5, Draw 11/4, City 6/4. O/U 2.5 quoted in one preview: Over 1.54 / Under 2.40 (~62% over implied).

team_news: Liverpool (Andoni Iraola): Alexander Isak (thigh, Sweden) and Cody Gakpo (ankle, Netherlands) reported ruled out by Iraola after international duty (earlier previews had them as late-decision doubts). Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni also sidelined. Likely front line built around Barcola centrally with Victor Munoz and Ngumoha/Wirtz; RotoWire pre-news XI: Alisson; Araujo, Gomez, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Munoz, Wirtz, Barcola. Man City (Enzo Maresca): Phil Foden suspended; Haaland limped off for Norway v Portugal but trained Thursday and Maresca says he is ready; Cherki expected at No.10; Semenyo expected on the left if ankle clears.
form_notes: City 5W from 5 (13-5), top on 15 pts, but margins narrow (1-0, 1-0, 2-1) apart from 4-1 at Palace and a 5-3 v Sunderland; conceded in 3 of 5. Liverpool unbeaten W2 D3 (7-4), 6th on 9 pts; draws 2-2 at Newcastle, 2-2 v Forest, 0-0 v Fulham; home record D2 (no home win yet). Iraola's Liverpool hard to beat; first Liverpool-City PL meeting without Klopp or Guardiola since 2015.
xg_notes: Per ats.io 5-game table: City xG 10.50 / xGA 7.18 (overperforming: 13 GF); Liverpool xG 8.34 / xGA 6.94 (7 GF). xG difference per game: City +0.66, Liverpool +0.28. Haaland scored in all 5 league games, 10 of 20 shots on target (RotoWire). Liverpool's xG likely depressed further by Isak/Gakpo/Ekitike absences.
pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC): Liverpool 1-2 Man City. RotoWire: 1-1. Another preview: 2-2. FreeTips: value on the draw at 11/4. ats.io: under 2.5. Jones Knows (Sky) column for this fixture not found.
reasoning: Opta (34.6/24.7/40.7) and the market (~35/26/39) both make City slight favourites, and City's xG difference (+0.66/game) is stronger than Liverpool's (+0.28). Liverpool losing Isak and Gakpo on top of Ekitike removes most of their centre-forward options, while City lose only Foden and have Haaland declared fit. I upweight the draw to 30% given the 32% season draw rate, Liverpool's three draws and that City's results are flattered by their xG. A rough Poisson (Liverpool ~1.3, City ~1.45 expected goals) makes 1-1 the single most likely score, but City win is the most likely result, and 1-2 fits Liverpool scoring in 4 of 5 and City conceding in 3 of 5.
risks: Haaland is not fully fit after limping off on international duty, and Liverpool's home crowd could make this a cagey 1-1 or 0-0. The injury reports conflict: earlier previews had Isak starting, so if he plays, Liverpool's chances go up.

opta.source: The Analyst Matchday 6 Opta supercomputer picks (published 8 Oct 2026), as summarised by search: Newcastle 44.8%, Coventry 29.8%. Draw not shown in the snippet; 25.4% is 100 minus the other two. A follow-up search could not independently re-confirm the figure.

odds.source: UK preview prices: Coventry 12/5, Draw 13/5, Newcastle 21/20 (de-vigged approx 28 / 26 / 46). DraftKings: Coventry +230, Draw +255, Newcastle +110. Squawka market: Newcastle 46%, draw 27%. Over 2.5 quoted around evens or slightly shorter.

team_news: Coventry: Taiwo Awoniyi suspended (red card v Brighton); Haji Wright injured (expected back later in October); Aurele Amenda, Josh Eccles (calf), Luke Woolfenden and Kaine Kesler-Hayden out; Milan van Ewijk back. Predicted XI (3-4-2-1): Rushworth; Pinnock, Thomas, Mfuni; van Ewijk, Onyeka, Grimes, Dasilva; Rudoni, Tchaouna/Mason-Clark; Thomas-Asante. Newcastle (reported as managed by Jaissle per LiveScore): Anthony Elanga (thigh) doubtful or out, depending on the source; Jacob Ramsey listed injured; Joelinton and Nico Gonzalez reported fit (Gonzalez cleared concussion protocol). Predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Gonzalez, Miley; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Wissa.
form_notes: Coventry (promoted) 18th, W1 L4, 1-10: lost 0-3 at Arsenal, 0-1 v Hull, 0-1 at City, 0-5 v Brighton, then won 1-0 at Forest in MW5. BTTS in none of their 5 games and only one goal scored, though four of the five opponents were strong. Newcastle 9th, W2 D2 L1, 9-9: 2-2 v Liverpool, 2-0 at Spurs, 2-2 v Bournemouth, 1-4 at Leeds, 2-1 v Hull. Four of their 5 games went over 2.5 goals, and they have one clean sheet.
xg_notes: OddAlerts xG table (5 games): Coventry xG 4.18 (0.84/game; 1 goal = heavy underperformance) and xGA 8.47; Newcastle xG 5.22 (1.04/game, while scoring 9 = overperformance) and xGA 9.92 (about 2/game, among the worst). On xG difference per game Newcastle (-0.94) are no better than Coventry (-0.86), and Coventry faced a much tougher schedule. Shots over the last 10 games (Gambling.com): Coventry 12.6 shots / 4.2 on target, Newcastle 12.7 / 4.5.
pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC): 1-1. RotoWire: 1-1. FreeSuperTips: 1-1. LiveScore: 1-1. Footballpredictions.com: 2-2. WhoScored: 0-2 (away win, under 2.5). Onside model: 1-2. Stats Insider: Newcastle 46.5%, best bet Under 2.5. Squawka: Newcastle win. Jones Knows not found.
reasoning: Opta (29.8/25.4/44.8) and the market (~28/26/46) favour Newcastle, but their underlying numbers are poor: about 1.0 xG for and 2.0 xGA per game, and their 9 goals well outstrip 5.2 xG. Coventry's xG is not much worse after a far harder schedule, so I trim Newcastle and push the draw to 31%, in line with the 32% season rate. I do not expect a heavy defeat for the promoted side. Coventry are missing both main forwards (Awoniyi suspended, Wright injured) and have scored once in five games, so a low-scoring Newcastle win is the most likely result. Rough expected goals of Coventry ~1.0 and Newcastle ~1.35 make 0-1 and 1-1 almost equally likely; 0-1 is the pick consistent with the most likely result.
risks: If the panel is short on draws, this is my preferred one to flip: 1-1 is near co-modal, and the consensus pick of Sutton, RotoWire and LiveScore. Coventry's xG suggests their finishing has to improve at some point, and Newcastle's leaky defence could give them the chance.
